haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds the image without pushing and runs unit tests; nothing deploys. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production deploy the same image, built once per merge run and tagged with the commit SHA. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration test failure gets one automatic retry, then if it fails again the run ends and is announced in #deploys. A unit test failure ends the run at once, with no retry, and is announced.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the previous_tag image after rollback; migrations stay applied. The image is found from the SSM Parameter Store previous_tag value for staging.
haiku-low.q5: Only members of the release-approvers group, not the merged commit's author. If nobody approves within 72 hours, the run expires, is announced in #deploys, and nothing reaches production.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store, as current_tag and previous_tag per environment. deploy.sh writes them only after a rollout succeeds. The canary is never recorded there.
haiku-low.q7: Stable keeps the old image, since it is not touched. Recorded tags are unchanged. The migration may stay applied, because migrations are forward-only and never undone.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is cancelled and not announced, if it is still waiting for approval, the window or the production lock. A run already in canary or stable production is never cancelled.
haiku-low.q9: Approved outside the window, it waits for the next opening and the approval stays valid. If another production deploy holds the lock, it waits for the lock within the window rules.
haiku-low.q10: The canary 5xx ratio from Prometheus is measured over the last minute, checked every minute for 15 minutes. Any reading above 1%, or no reading returned, counts as a failure.
haiku-low.q12: Staging: kubectl rollout undo if the rollout started; production: rollout undo on stable plus canary-off. It returns to the previous revision, which should match SSM current_tag because tags are written only after success.

sonnet.q1: A PR runs checks: builds the image (no push) and runs unit tests (make test-unit); it never deploys. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Each merge run builds one image tagged with the commit SHA, pushed to registry.internal/shop-api; staging and production deploy that same image. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: retried once automatically; if it fails again the run ends and failure is announced in #deploys. Unit test failure: no retry; run ends and failure is announced.
sonnet.q4: deploy.sh rollback staging restores the image from SSM previous_tag for staging, so staging runs the previous image. The run ends, failure announced; the migration stays applied.
sonnet.q5: A member of the release-approvers group who is not the author of the merged commit. If no one approves within 72 h of staging smoke tests passing, the run expires, expiry is announced in #deploys, and nothing reaches production.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: current_tag and previous_tag per environment, kept by deploy.sh. Written only after the rollout succeeds. The repo keeps no live state and the canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment is not touched (canary-off is run). SSM tags are not written. The database migration stays applied (may stay applied if the canary deploy itself failed); migrations are never undone.
sonnet.q8: When the newer run is approved, the older run still waiting for approval, window or production lock is superseded: cancelled and not announced. (Document does not say what happens at the moment the newer run merely passes staging, before approval.) An older run already in canary or stable production is never cancelled.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it waits for the next window opening and its approval stays valid (no expiry while waiting). While another production deploy is in progress: it waits for the production lock, also subject to the window check.
sonnet.q10: The canary 5xx ratio (5xx http_requests_total rate for app=shop-api-canary divided by total rate for it, over the last minute), read from Prometheus by the pipeline run every minute for 15 minutes. Failure: any reading above 1%, or no reading returned.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. (Document says only that approval is a CI job that waits for a person and gives no notification mechanism or decision information; announcements in #deploys cover only failures, expiries and finished production deploys.)
sonnet.q12: Run kubectl rollout undo on the deployment (in staging if the rollout started; on stable in production, plus deploy.sh canary-off). It returns to the previous revision, which should match SSM current_tag because tags are written only after success. Whether this holds after earlier rollbacks is an open question. Migrations are not undone.
